newsitem.title: USA: ISI Company Survey Index 50.9 week ended Aug 15.
newsitem.headline: ISI Company Survey Index 50.9 week ended Aug 15.

text.p: The International Strategy & Investment (ISI) Group Inc said its Company Survey Index fell to 50.9 for the week ended August 15 from 53.6 in the prior week.
The four-week moving average inched up to 52.1 from 52.0 for the same period, ISI said.
Effective next Monday, ISI said its Company Survey Index will be available for public release at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT.

"While our Company Survey Index fell in the latest week, the four-week moving average continues to show that the economy has accelerated in the third quarter and that August is stronger than July," said Jason Trennert, vice president at ISI.
In addition, Trennert said, "The survey indicates that, at least through last week, there was little overall impact of the UPS strike on the economy."
The Teamsters Union strike at UPS entered its third week on Monday with the company and the union closer to a settlement than they were four days ago, UPS chairman James Kelly said earlier Monday.
ISI Group surveys about 100 companies weekly including retailers, auto dealers, manufacturers, homebuilders, and banks.
The Company Survey Index is based on a scale from 0=weak to 100=strong and is meant to be a current measure of economic strength.
